title: Remember me at the altar (9.11)
hookLine: dying, Monica asks only to be remembered at the Lord's altar
tomorrow: what is a person actually loving when they love God?

cards: A candle in red glass, flickering by a side altar. A name said aloud during the prayers at Mass. Monica's last request is about a moment like that.
Not long after the window at Ostia, she falls ill, far from her home in Africa. Friends ask whether she isn't afraid to be buried so far from her own city.
Her answer: nothing is far from God, and there's no fear he won't know where to raise her up at the end of the world. Then she tells her sons the one thing she wants.

teach.b: First, the request. Lay this body anywhere, she says, and don't let the care of it trouble you. Then, in her Latin as Augustine gives it: tantum illud vos rogo, ut ad domini altare memineritis mei, ubi fueritis.
This only I ask of you, that you remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you are. Second, the change. Augustine is surprised.
She had long planned to lie beside her husband, and had prepared a grave next to his. Now she lets it go without a fight. Third, what the altar means.
For Monica the altar is the Eucharist, and to be remembered there is to be prayed for at Mass.
Augustine says that when she was buried, the sacrifice of our redemption was offered for her. Fourth, the turn at the end of book nine. Augustine looks up from the page and speaks to his readers.

He asks whoever reads his words to remember Monica and her husband, Patricius, at the altar. So a request made to her sons in a port town is passed to every reader of the book, and that includes whoever is listening now.

how: Catholics pray for the dead at Mass, naming them in the Eucharistic Prayer's remembrance of the departed, and a family can ask a priest to offer a Mass for someone who has died.

games.q: what does “remember me at the altar” mean?
o: Augustine's vow to build a church for her
Monica's request to be prayed for at Mass
a plea to be buried in her home town

p: Monica, on dying far from home
prepared beside her husband, let go
where she asked to be remembered
asked to remember Monica and Patricius

s: Monica insisted on being buried beside her husband
she had prepared that grave, then let it go: lay this body anywhere.
Augustine asks his readers to remember Monica and Patricius at the altar
at the end of book nine, so the request reaches every reader.
Monica was afraid of dying far from her own city
nothing is far from God, she said.

games.q: a friend feels guilty she can't visit her dad's grave across the country. what does Monica's last request offer her?
o: nothing is far from God; remembering him in prayer goes anywhere.
she should move closer, since the grave is what matters most.
remembering only really counts at the grave itself.
games.why: Monica let go of the grave she had prepared. Lay this body anywhere, she said; only remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you are.

practice: Bring to mind one person who has died, and say their name aloud, softly, once. If you go to Mass, you can carry that name to the altar the way Catholics do; if not, let the sound of the name stay in the room a little longer.
If grief is heavy right now, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US you can call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Remember me at the altar. Monica's one request as she was dying: not a grave beside her husband, but prayer at the Lord's altar.

orig.note: Latin, Confessions 9.11: remember me at the Lord's altar.

carryVoice: Remember me at the altar: a name, carried to Mass, from wherever you happen to be. Go in peace.
